identity: Scripture. The complete text of Surat al-Balad (Quran 90), all 20 ayat, in Uthmani orthography with the diacritics and the verse markers stripped -- the spellings give it away: الإنسن for الإنسان، هدينه for هديناه، أصحب for أصحاب، بايتنا for بآياتنا، المشمة for المشأمة، plus فى and ذى. One single paragraph, no <NL> tokens anywhere, 82 tokens indexed 0-81, ending at مؤصدة.
law: The AYA is the sentence. A Quranic source carries exactly one punctuation-like mark, the verse separator ۝; so 'punctuation REMOVED' means the aya separators were removed, and the gold boundaries stand exactly where they stood. This is the formal-unit law my doctrine already holds for the two adjacent genres: K1 (verse -- metrical form, not syntax, sets the boundary, and the short-tail brake 0b is suspended) and L1 (isnad -- حدثنا إسماعيل stands alone as a two-word unit). Formal unit beats syntactic unit, and it beats it in BOTH directions: a two-word aya (فك رقبة) is a full unit, and a nine-token aya is NOT split at its internal finite connectives however heavy they are. Consequence for this document: 20 ayat, 20 units, no unit boundary anywhere inside an aya.
reasoning: The whole document turns on a single choice -- aya granularity versus syntactic-clause granularity -- and a mixed answer would score worse than either pure reading, so I commit to the aya line throughout and accept its cost at every site. (1) Most boundaries are overdetermined, being simultaneously verse-ends and independent-predication breaks, so both readings agree: @3 (وأنت حل = own subject+predicate, A1), @10 (before لقد), @15, @21, @25, @30, @36 (وهدينه = new finite verb), @38 (فلا = clause-initial ف, B1), @41 (وما أدريك = own predication), @45, @60 (ثم = CUT in my table), @69 (أولئك opens a new nominal sentence), @72 (والذين كفروا = own predication, contrastive parallel), @78 (عليهم نار مؤصدة = own nominal predication). (2) THE RISKIEST CUT, @34 عينين | ولسانا وشفتين. This is the sharpest conflict in the document. ولسانا وشفتين is a bare-noun conjunct pair of two words -- exactly the shape the §0 conjunct-weight test says NOT to cut and exactly the shape the short-tail rule 0b absorbs; compare السمع والبصر والشم in doc_66c98646b9a9 and الأمزجة والصلابة واللين in B2, both of which stay whole. Prose doctrine says merge. Aya 9 says cut. I take the cut: the formal-unit law governs this genre, and since the two readings put symmetric risk on this one site, my ~7:1 under-segmentation bias breaks the tie toward cutting. (3) @7 البلد | ووالد وما ولد -- the same conflict, milder. ووالد is a bare noun on the oath, which prose logic would absorb, but it is the third parallel oath-object in a row (بهذا البلد / وأنت حل بهذا البلد / ووالد وما ولد), and B2 says parallelism defeats the short-tail rule. Aya 3 and B2 agree; cut. (4) @47 رقبة is only two words and would normally be absorbed, but 0b is suspended in formal-unit genres (K1, I3), and independently the conjunct that follows, أو إطعم فى يوم ذى مسغبة, carries its own PP frame, so the conjunct-weight test cuts here on its own terms. (5) @53 مسغبة | يتيما ذا مقربة is asyndetic and يتيما is grammatically the direct object of إطعام, so pure syntax would merge; but aya 15 cuts, and it is supported by the matching sibling أو مسكينا ذا متربة -- two same-shaped siblings, the I4/B2 parallelism signal. Same reasoning carries @56. (6) THE RECIPROCAL TEST, which is what keeps this answer honest. Aya 17, ثم كان من الذين ءامنوا وتواصوا بالصبر وتواصوا بالمرحمة, runs nine tokens and contains two finite وتواصوا clauses; A1 and the conjunct-weight test would cut before وتواصوا بالمرحمة (finite verb plus its own PP). I hold it as ONE unit, because it is one aya. Likewise no cut inside ووالد وما ولد (aya 3) despite the verb ولد, and none inside أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد. Applying the formal law means accepting it where it REMOVES cuts, not only where it adds them; a version of this answer that took the aya cuts but also took the internal A1 cuts would be incoherent. (7) Structure: there are no <NL> tokens, so the only mechanically guaranteed boundary is the final token @81 مؤصدة, which is also the end of aya 20 -- consistent with the reading. Confidence key below: hi = aya boundary that is also an independent syntactic break (both laws agree); med = aya boundary carried by the formal law alone, against what prose doctrine would do.
